text: Section: Ongoing Research Projects Design and Development of an Optical (SPR) Biosensor for the Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases in Humans This project focuses on the development of a surface plasmon resonance (SPR)-based optical biosensor for detecting infectious diseases in humans. The sensor leverages the high sensitivity of SPR technology to identify biomarkers in biological samples. The non-invasive approach ensures faster diagnostics with minimal patient discomfort. The design is aimed at achieving portability, making it suitable for use in diverse healthcare settings. The innovation promises to improve early disease detection and patient outcomes. Optical Sensor for Chromium Detection in Remote and Rural Waterbodies & Industry Water Outlet for Net Zero Discharge, and their Field Testing This project develops an optical sensor tailored to detect chromium contamination in water sources, including rural waterbodies and industrial outlets, which are carcinogenic in nature. The sensor ensures real-time detection of chromium levels, aiding in regulatory compliance for net-zero discharge policies. Field testing validates its effectiveness in diverse environments. The portable design facilitates deployment in remote areas lacking laboratory infrastructure. This initiative promotes environmental protection and sustainable water

Students should have strong mathematical and analytical skills to understand how machines can be used as drivers of innovation. This course is for those who are looking for a cutting-edge exploration of physics, mathematics, and thermodynamics to create machines and technologies that drive innovation across borders and sectors. text: Section: Department of Mechanical Engineering leaps and bounds since its inception, with the current undergraduate intake at 120. The department is housed in a well-equipped three-floor building with excellent infrastructure. It features state-of-the-art laboratories including CAD, Metallography and Materials Testing, Metrology, Foundry and Forging, Machine Shop, Fluid Mechanics, Heat Transfer, Energy Engineering, and Design labs. Advanced computing facilities and industry-standard software enhance student learning. The department is led by Dr. Vinay K B, Head of the Department, and guided by experienced faculty specializing in Thermal, Design, Production, and Engineering Management with 26 PhD holders and 12 faculty pursuing doctoral studies, ensuring strong teaching and research excellence. The department provides excellent placement opportunities through strong industry interaction, training, and career support. It regularly organizes expert talks and industrial visits to enhance students' theoretical knowledge and practical exposure. Conferences and workshops are conducted to strengthen technical expertise. text: Section: The Department of Physics Welcome to the Department of Physics at VVCE, Mysuru. The Department of Physics was established in the year 1997. The Department not only offers the students to explore fundamental physics but also promote interdisciplinary research work. The Department is working hard towards providing innovative and quality education through its dedicated and experienced teaching faculty members. The research work of the Department is contributing strongly across disciplines that include Material Science, Semi-Conductor devices, Reliability Studies, Cryogenic Properties, Nanomaterials, Crystallography, Polymers etc. The department is committed to fostering scientific curiosity and academic excellence.

text: Section: The Department of Chemistry The department of Chemistry started in the year 1997 and engaged in teaching applied chemistry to the first year students of all branches in engineering. The department has highly qualified, dedicated and experienced faculties, presently headed by Dr. Anitha Sudhir. The department aims to impart high quality education, inspiring students to compete globally and to develop scientific outlook with analytical mind. The faculty members attend FDP, Workshops and Seminars to upgrade their knowledge. Department has R&D center recognized by VTU, Belagavi. The faculties involve both in teaching as well as research and publish research papers in various national and international journals. At present, four faculties are guiding the students for Ph.D degree and have applied for the project.

text: Section: The Department of Mathematics The department of Mathematics was established in the year 1997, with a modest strength of 3 faculty members. It has grown in strength and now boasts of having a team of 26 well qualified and experienced teaching faculty members of which 20 have Ph.D. and 8 are pursuing their Ph.D. program. The department has to its credit several quality papers published in National and International journals of repute. The members of the department have been invited to deliver guest lectures at various reputed institution. The department conducts courses on Engineering Mathematics for UG, Advanced Mathematics for PG and Bridge courses for lateral entry students. Special classes are conducted for the academically weak students to enable them to perform well. The department has been consistently obtaining good results due the sincere efforts of the team. Apart from academics, all the staff members are involved in various co-curricular and extra-curricular activities. The Department has a well-furnished Research Centre established in 2011. At present, the centre has 7 recognized research supervisors and 15 research scholars, including two full-time scholars pursuing Ph.D.

text: Section: Library & Information Center The Vidyavardhaka College of Engineering Library was founded in 1997. All activities on campus revolve around the library, which is the center of the institution. Located on the seventh level of the Administrative Block, this 1400 square meter space houses the digital library, reference library, and circulation section. The library is carefully developed and enhanced. There are 8700 titles in its collection of over 45,000 books. In addition to providing access to more than 26,000 ebooks and 17,000 journals, the library subscribes to about 87 hardcopy journals. Every document has been categorized using Dewey Decimal Classification (DDC) and AACR II, and it has been methodically stored on Open Access. There are 350 seats available for reading at the library. Daily library operations include acquisition, cataloguing, serial control, circulation, and OPAC. The main library is automated with KOHA integrated library automation software and is RFID-equipped. The library features a server with thirty desktop computers and a Wi-Fi connection.

In addition, a qualifying rank in either PGCET/GATE is a must. Out of the total seats, 80% is filled through KEA and 20% through Management quota. MBA For admissions to the MBA Program, the minimum percentage in eligibility examination of Bachelor’s degree in BBM/B.Com/B.Sc/BA/BE is 50% for General Merit (GM) candidates and 45% for SC, ST, Cat-1, 2A, 2B, 3A and 3B category candidates. text: Section: Frequently Asked Questions — Is there any enterance exam to get enrolled into Engineering programs? Is there any enterance exam to get enrolled into Engineering programs? Yes. | A candidate who has passed the Qualifying Exam (Q.E.) namely PUC/12th grade/10+2 with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects along with Chemistry / Bio-Technology / Biology / Electronics / Computer Science as optional subjects with English as one of the languages of study and obtained an aggregate minimum of 45% marks in the optional subjects in the Q.E. is eligible for Engineering / Technological courses and 40% of marks in the Q.E. in case of SC, ST, Category-I and OBC (2A, 2B, 3A and 3B) category candidates. text: Section: Academic Collaborations Overview Collaboration between industry and academia offers a fusion of practical expertise and academic rigor to organizations. The primary goal of the committee is to bridge the gap between academia and industry by understanding and addressing the industrial needs of the region. This involves providing industrial exposure to faculty and students to align their knowledge with industrial practices. Efforts include identifying industrial partners for establishing Centers of Excellence, organizing collaborative workshops and conferences, and facilitating joint projects and dissertation work supervised by both faculty and industry experts. Additionally, faculty expertise is leveraged to offer consultancy and solve industry challenges, while in-plant training opportunities are provided for students to gain practical experience.

text: VIDYAVARDHAKA COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING/Intellectual Property Rights Policy VVCE VIDYAVARDHAKA COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING Inspire Innovate Implement Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Cell VIDYAVARDHAKA COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING ( a unit of Vidyavardhaka Sangha ® , Mysuru) GOKULAM 3rd STAGE, MYSURU-570 002 VIDYAVARDHAKA COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING/Intellectual Property Rights Policy POLICY FOR INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY FILING AND PROTECTION INTRODUCTION Intellectual Property Rights are exclusive legal rights over creations of the mind. IPR give the proprietor rights to exploit intellectual creation of the mind. IPRs are essential to fostering innovation to encourage inventiveness in various areas of research and development. It contributes to ensure profitability and better service to the society. PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVE The principal objectives of Vidyavardhaka College of Engineering’s IPR Policy are:  To encourage creative and innovative research leading to the generation of new knowledge, ideas and inventions.  To facilitate the transfer of Vidyavardhaka College of Engineering (VVCE) -developed research results and new knowledge of commerce and industry.  To provide faculty mem bers, staff and students of VVCE assistance in assessin g the patentability and commercial potential of their inventions. 
title: vvce_ipr.pdf

text: (VVCE) -developed research results and new knowledge of commerce and industry.  To provide faculty mem bers, staff and students of VVCE assistance in assessin g the patentability and commercial potential of their inventions.  To train faculty members, staff and students about provisional patent filing procedures in India as well as the procedure for filing the Applications under the Patent Cooperation Treaty  To make faculty members, staff and students familiar with Patent filing forms (Form - 1,2 & 5)  To make faculty members, staff and students aware about the various requirements/data to be provided for filling of such forms.  To facilitate the filing of applicatio ns and licensing where prima facie the VVCE finds it patentable. SCOPE OF THE POLICY 1. IPR cell shall guide and help the faculty members and students of VVCE in patentability assessment and to apply for various IPRs such as Invention(s), Designs, Integrated Circuit Layouts and other creative works. 2. The faculty members/students desirous of filing a patent or for any other IPR application would be given the necessary advice and

text: 1 THE CODE OF CONDUCT FOR TEACHERS I. TEACHERS AND THEIR RESPONSIBILITIES: Whoever adopts teaching as a profession assumes the obligation to conduct himself in accordance with the ideals of the profession. A teacher is constantly under the scrutiny of his students and the society at large. Therefore, every teacher should see that there is no incompatibility between his precepts and practice. The national ideals of education which have already been set forth and which he/she should seek to inculcate among students must be his/her own ideals. The profession further requires that the teachers should be calm, patient, and communicative by temperament and amiable in disposition. Teachers should: (i) adhere to a responsible pattern of conduct and demeanour expected of them by the community; (ii) manage their private affairs in a manner consistent with the dignity of the profession; (iii) seek to make professional growth continuous through study and research; (iv) express free and fran k opinion by participation at professional meetings, seminars, conferences etc. towards the contribution of knowledge; (v) maintain active membership of professional organisations and strive to

text: Education for Realising the Aspirations articulated in NEP2020 3 Abstract The new education policy has come with great clarity on the expectations from education. It states that “education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and just society, and promoting national development”. That means the graduates coming out of our educational institutions must have the commitment and competence to work on and realise the aspirations articulated in NEP2020. The policy calls for a bold implementation plan which has universal human values as well as Indian culture and ethos (IKS) at the centre. The essence being humaneness, human consciousness and well-being of all. So, if we work out the vision, mission and values of the proposed education system, it will look something like this: Vision: To realise an equitable and just society as well as promoting national development (making India a global knowledge leader). Mission: To develop graduates to their full human potential (human consciousness, human conduct), who will be committed to national development and global well-being in a collaborative manner with all concerned agencies. text: Section: Parampara About the Club PARAMPARA, Dept. cultural club provides a space beyond the classroom—a space to discover talents, express creativity, build confidence and celebrate our diverse cultural heritage. The club is envisioned as a platform where every talent gets an opportunity, every student gets a voice, and every culture gets an opportunity to be celebrated. Club Objectives A aims to celebrate the diversity of our student community and build a cultural tradition that can be carried forward from one generation of students to the next. It is about giving talent a platform, creativity a voice, and students a space to connect and celebrate. The Department of CSE inaugurated PARAMPARA – CSE Cultural Club on 7 September 2026, providing students with a vibrant platform to showcase their talents and celebrate cultural heritage. The event was graced by the Principal, Vice-Principal, HOD, Deputy Heads, faculty members, and students. The inauguration featured the ceremonial lamp lighting, presentation of the club objectives, and the launch of the PARAMPARA logo. As part of the event, the department also celebrated Teachers’ Day with a cake

text: Section: Department of Computer Science & Engineering Is for students… who are innovative thinkers and for those who want to master the world of technology. Students should have strong mathematical and analytical skills to understand how digital technologies can be used as drivers of innovation. This course provides a cutting-edge exploration of programming, mathematics, and analytics to create out-of-the-box designs with digital technologies necessary to drive innovation across borders and sectors. To Become… - a cybersecurity specialist - a blockchain developer - a data scientist - an augmented reality developer Nothing is exciting in these times as the field of Computer Science. Being close to India’s Silicon Valley, young bright students are eager to pursue their graduation courses in this field. Ever since its inception in 1997, the department has been a pioneering academic center for under graduation and post-graduation in the areas of Computer Science Engineering. It has assiduously pursued its mission of carrying out leading edge facilities in both foundational and Industry oriented problems. The Department has well qualified & dedicated faculty members. The department is well equipped with state of art infrastructure
title: Department of Computer Science & Engineering – Vidyavardhaka College of Engineering

text: Section: Department of Computer Science & Engineering pursued its mission of carrying out leading edge facilities in both foundational and Industry oriented problems. The Department has well qualified & dedicated faculty members. The department is well equipped with state of art infrastructure with latest computers, Laboratory Equipment’s, 1 Gbps leased line connection & Wi-Fi Internet connectivity. Student clubs like Code club, Developer Student club, Open Source Community and Student chapters including ACM student chapter, IEEE student chapter, promote holistic development of the students. Department has industry collaboration with Google Cloud Platform, AWS, Github, UIpath etc., Research collaboration with STKOM University Indonesia, Providence University Taiwan, North Dakota State University, etc., also associated with premier institute like IITs and NITs. The academic programs of the Department are highly innovative and keenly sought after. The Department has trained more than a thousand engineers who have distinguished themselves as leading academicians, industry professionals, and entrepreneurs in several universities and industries in India and abroad.

text: Section: Department of Computer Science & Engineering (AI & ML) Is for students… who are innovative thinkers and for those who want to master the world of technology. Students should have strong mathematical and analytical skills to understand how digital technologies can be used as drivers of innovation. This course provides a cutting-edge exploration of programming, mathematics, and analytics to create out-of-the-box designs with digital technologies necessary to drive innovation across borders and sectors. Why Aritificial Intelligence & Machine Learning? Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a new and upcoming program in the area of computer science that is rapidly expanding its boundaries to variety of fields like healthcare, security, entertainment, education, autonomous transportation, intelligent robots, space exploration, speech processing, stock trading and many more. AI and its applications have brought significant changes in our lives. AI tries to bring in intelligence into machines artificially by mimicking the human intelligence. text: Section: Career Path Possibilities Electronics and Communication Engineering is a versatile and ever-evolving field that plays a crucial role in modern technology and communication systems. It offers students a robust foundation and a multitude of opportunities to innovate and excel in various industries. The usefulness of an ECE degree enables graduates to explore careers in various sectors, including telecommunications, information technology, consumer electronics, healthcare, and more. Continuous learning and staying updated with technological advancements are key to thriving in these dynamic fields. Through a commitment to quality education, research, and adaptation to emerging trends, ECE departments continue to produce professionals who contribute significantly to various technological sectors, driving progress and development in the modern world. text: Section: Year 1: Foundational Coursework - In the initial years, students focus on building a strong foundation in mathematics, physics, and basic engineering principles. - Courses often include Social Innovation projects and engineering exploration labs , and introductory programming. These subjects are crucial for understanding complex ECE concepts in later years. - Also students are encouraged to join various students clubs and gain experience.
title: Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering – Vidyavardhaka College of Engineering

text: Section: Year 2: Core ECE Courses As students progress, they delve into core ECE subjects such as electronic circuits, signals and systems, digital logic design, and microprocessors and controllers and also they are provided with various TPEC and GPEC courses. These courses provide essential knowledge specific to electronics and communication engineering. Laboratory Work and Practical Experience (Throughout the Program) Hands-on laboratory sessions complement theoretical learning, allowing students to apply concepts in real-world scenarios. Access to well-equipped student laboratories enables independent and collaborative projects, fostering practical skills essential for engineering practice.
title: Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering – Vidyavardhaka College of Engineering

text: Section: Year 3: Elective Courses and Specializations In the later stages of the program, students can choose open electives and professional electives that align with their interests and career goals. High-achieving students may participate in honours programs or undergraduate research opportunities, engaging in advanced projects that contribute to the field and enhance their academic experience. This flexibility allows students to tailor their education to specific fields within ECE.
title: Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering – Vidyavardhaka College of Engineering

text: Section: Year 4: Capstone and Career Preparation The culmination of the ECE program often involves a capstone project where students work in teams to design, develop, and implement a complex engineering solution. This project integrates the knowledge and skills acquired throughout the program and demonstrates readiness for professional practice. Gaining practical experience through internships is highly encouraged, providing exposure to industry practices and enhancing employability. Internships allow students to apply academic knowledge in professional settings, develop industry-relevant skills, and build professional networks. Graduation and Awards: Upon successful completion of all academic requirements, students graduate with a Bachelor’s degree in ECE. Outstanding students may receive departmental awards recognizing academic excellence and contributions to the field.

This advancement heralded the new era of Information Technology in which we live. This discipline has given plethora of versatile gadgets and reliable systems that has made the lives of this generation easy.

text: Section: Ongoing Research Projects Design and Development of an Optical (SPR) Biosensor for the Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases in Humans This project focuses on the development of a surface plasmon resonance (SPR)-based optical biosensor for detecting infectious diseases in humans. The sensor leverages the high sensitivity of SPR technology to identify biomarkers in biological samples. The non-invasive approach ensures faster diagnostics with minimal patient discomfort. The design is aimed at achieving portability, making it suitable for use in diverse healthcare settings. The innovation promises to improve early disease detection and patient outcomes. Optical Sensor for Chromium Detection in Remote and Rural Waterbodies & Industry Water Outlet for Net Zero Discharge, and their Field Testing This project develops an optical sensor tailored to detect chromium contamination in water sources, including rural waterbodies and industrial outlets, which are carcinogenic in nature. The sensor ensures real-time detection of chromium levels, aiding in regulatory compliance for net-zero discharge policies. Field testing validates its effectiveness in diverse environments. The portable design facilitates deployment in remote areas lacking laboratory infrastructure. This initiative promotes environmental protection and sustainable water
title: Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering – Vidyavardhaka College of Engineering

text: Section: Ongoing Research Projects aiding in regulatory compliance for net-zero discharge policies. Field testing validates its effectiveness in diverse environments. A Portable UV-Vis Device for Polyethylene Microplastic Detection: Empowering Sustainable Water Monitoring This project involves the creation of a portable UV-Vis spectroscopic device for detecting polyethylene microplastics in water. The device is designed for affordability and accuracy, providing real-time monitoring of water pollution. By targeting polyethylene, it addresses a significant contributor to plastic contamination. The compact system empowers environmental scientists and policymakers to assess and mitigate water pollution effectively. The innovation supports sustainable water management efforts and raises awareness about microplastic pollution.

text: Section: Ongoing Research Projects Design and Development of an Optical (SPR) Biosensor for the Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases in Humans This project focuses on the development of a surface plasmon resonance (SPR)-based optical biosensor for detecting infectious diseases in humans. The sensor leverages the high sensitivity of SPR technology to identify biomarkers in biological samples. The non-invasive approach ensures faster diagnostics with minimal patient discomfort. The design is aimed at achieving portability, making it suitable for use in diverse healthcare settings. The innovation promises to improve early disease detection and patient outcomes. Optical Sensor for Chromium Detection in Remote and Rural Waterbodies & Industry Water Outlet for Net Zero Discharge, and their Field Testing This project develops an optical sensor tailored to detect chromium contamination in water sources, including rural waterbodies and industrial outlets, which are carcinogenic in nature. The sensor ensures real-time detection of chromium levels, aiding in regulatory compliance for net-zero discharge policies. Field testing validates its effectiveness in diverse environments. The portable design facilitates deployment in remote areas lacking laboratory infrastructure. This initiative promotes environmental protection and sustainable water
title: Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering – Vidyavardhaka College of Engineering

text: Section: Department of Electrical & Electronics Engineering The Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE) Department combines the principles of electrical engineering and electronics to address the evolving technological needs of society. It focuses on areas such as power systems, control systems, embedded systems, and renewable energy, while fostering innovation in emerging fields like electric vehicles, smart grids, and IoT-based solutions. With a well-structured curriculum, modern laboratories, and experienced faculty, the department emphasizes hands-on learning, research, and industry collaboration. By equipping students with technical skills, critical thinking, and ethical values, the department aims to produce competent professionals capable of driving technological advancements and contributing to sustainable development. Career Opportunities - An Electrical Engineer - A Design Engineer - A Control and - Instrumentation Engineer - An automation Engineer The Department of Electrical & Electronics Engineering started in 2004. It offers B.E and Ph.D. programs. The Department aims at providing quality education to the students. This course is for those who are looking for a cutting-edge exploration of physics, mathematics, and thermodynamics to create machines and technologies that drive innovation across borders and sectors. text: Section: Department of Mechanical Engineering leaps and bounds since its inception, with the current undergraduate intake at 120. The department is housed in a well-equipped three-floor building with excellent infrastructure. It features state-of-the-art laboratories including CAD, Metallography and Materials Testing, Metrology, Foundry and Forging, Machine Shop, Fluid Mechanics, Heat Transfer, Energy Engineering, and Design labs. Advanced computing facilities and industry-standard software enhance student learning. The department is led by Dr. Vinay K B, Head of the Department, and guided by experienced faculty specializing in Thermal, Design, Production, and Engineering Management with 26 PhD holders and 12 faculty pursuing doctoral studies, ensuring strong teaching and research excellence. The department provides excellent placement opportunities through strong industry interaction, training, and career support. It regularly organizes expert talks and industrial visits to enhance students' theoretical knowledge and practical exposure. Conferences and workshops are conducted to strengthen technical expertise. text: Electric Vehicle Centre of Excellence (EV-COE) About: With the rapid transition of the automotive industry towards electric mobility, there is an urgent need to equip our students with industry-relevant skills and practical exposure. The Centre of Excellence aims to bridge the gap between academic learning and industrial requirements in EV technology. Electric vehicles (EVs) operate using an electric powertrain that converts electrical energy stored in batteries into mechanical energy to drive the motor. The power ON/OFF sequence ensures safe activation of the system, where a pre -charge circuit limits i nrush current and protects components. Voltage and current behavior vary under no -load and load conditions, influencing overall system performance and efficiency. Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM) are commonly used due to their high efficiency and torque characteristics. Regenerative braking improves energy efficiency by converting kinetic energy back into electrical energy and storing it in the battery. The performance of lithium-ion cells is evaluated through tests such as open circuit voltage (OCV), capacity measurement, and discharge at different C -rates. Battery efficiency is analyzed using coulombic and round -trip efficiency
title: Electric-Vehicle-Centre-of-Excellence.pdf

text: the battery. The performance of lithium-ion cells is evaluated through tests such as open circuit voltage (OCV), capacity measurement, and discharge at different C -rates. Battery efficiency is analyzed using coulombic and round -trip efficiency measurements. Internal resistance (DCIR) affects heat generation and efficiency of the battery. The Battery Management S ystem (BMS) plays a crucial role in monitoring voltage, current, and temperature to ensure safe operation. It also provides protection against overvoltage, overcurrent, and temperature extremes while estimating the state of charge using methods like OCV an d coulomb counting. Objectives of the Centre of Excellence • To provide hands-on practical training in EV powertrain and Battery Management Systems (BMS). • To enhance employability, internships, and placement opportunities • To develop the institution as a regional skill hub for EV technology • To provide hands-on training in Battery Management Systems through a MAT lab to meet industrial application requirements. text: Section: Department of Civil Engineering The Department of Civil Engineering was incepted in the year 2013 with a sanctioned intake of 60 (UG)students and in 2025 M.Tech in Civil Engineering was sanctioned with an Intake of 18 students. Dr. Shilpa B S, In-Charge Head of the department is leading with experienced and dedicated faculty members having different specializations in Civil Engineering. | Five faculty members in the department are having doctoral degree, Eleven faculty members are working for Ph.D. Vision To be globally recognized in civil engineering education and research, promoting sustainability, innovation and ethics for societal needs. Mission 1: To provide comprehensive education and industry exposure through advanced infrastructure and skilled faculty. 2: To foster research, innovation and industry collaboration for addressing real- world challenges. 3: To empower students with knowledge, skill and personality for sustainable growth. Equipped with mineral samples, including rock and ore-forming, Structural Models, and Geological Maps Surveying Lab Equipped with a sophisticated Theodolite and a Total station. CAD Lab Equipped with new higher-end computer systems (76Nos), Autodesk Autocad and STAAD Pro V8i Software with 25 KVA online UP Hydraulics and Hydraulics Machinery Lab Closed circuit lab equipped with Centrifugal Pump, Pelton Wheel, Kaplan Turbine, Venturimeter, Hydraulic Flume and Bernoulli’s Apparatus and many more. text: the Programme: Corporate valuation has become one of the most critical competencies for finance professionals, academicians, consultants, investors, and corporate decision-makers. Understanding how businesses create value and applying appropriate valuation techniques are essential for informed strategic and financial decisions. This Management Development Programme (MDP) is designed to strengthen participants' conceptual understanding and practical application of corporate valuation techniques. The programme integrates financial statement analysis, valuation models, value driver assessment, and hands-on valuation exercises using real-world business cases. Participants will gain practical exposure to contemporary valuation methodologies widely used in investment banking, equity research, mergers and acquisitions, consulting, venture capital, and corporate finance. Programme Objectives: Strengthen participants' understanding of financial statement analysis and its application in evaluating corporate performance. Provide hands-on exposure to business valuation approaches including Discounted Cash Flow (DCF), Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF), Free Cash Flow to Equity (FCFE), Relative Valuation, and Value Driver Analysis. Enable participants to integrate valuation concepts into teaching, research, consulting, and industry-oriented academic activities. Balaji Kannan is a distinguished academician, researcher, trainer and administrator with more than 24 years of combined experience in higher education and industry. He has previously served as Chairperson of the Department of Commerce & Management at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Mysuru Campus, where he successfully led multidisciplinary academic programmes, curriculum development, faculty mentoring and accreditation initiatives. His doctoral research focuses on Business Sustainability, while his academic interests encompass Corporate Finance, Business Valuation, Financial Markets, Financial Distress Prediction, Sustainability and Public–Private Partnerships. His scholarly contributions include numerous publications in Scopus-indexed and ABDC-listed journals, reflecting his commitment to impactful research. Before entering academia, he worked with Cognizant and Polaris Software Lab, gaining valuable industry experience in finance, treasury and management information systems. Inaugurated under the theme | “Students Shaping Success,” | the club embodies a vision where education goes beyond classrooms—fostering future leaders who are not only academically sound but also equipped with real-world managerial skills. Derived from Sanskrit, | ‘Nirvaaha’ | means | effective execution or management | , reflecting the club’s commitment to excellence in thought and action. It also signifies the | collective journey of students managing ideas, resources, and aspirations | to achieve purposeful success. Driven by the belief that | students are not just learners but leaders in the making | , the club embodies the vision of shaping future-ready professionals who create value wherever they go.
